headline: New York City's Click-to-Cancel Rule Takes Effect
meta_description: New York City enforces a new rule making it as easy to cancel subscriptions as it is to sign up, protecting consumers from trapped contracts.
summary_short: New York City has enacted a groundbreaking rule requiring companies to make subscription cancellations as simple as the sign-up process itself.
body:
New York City has enacted a groundbreaking rule requiring companies to make subscription cancellations as simple as the sign-up process itself. The click-to-cancel regulation takes effect, shifting power back to consumers who have long struggled with deliberately complicated cancellation procedures.

This policy addresses a widespread frustration: signing up for services typically takes seconds through a simple button click, yet canceling often requires multiple steps, phone calls, or buried menu options. New York City's intervention aims to eliminate this imbalance, forcing businesses to offer the same frictionless exit that they offer entry.

The rule represents a practical consumer protection measure, acknowledging that subscription traps harm families and individuals. By requiring symmetry between sign-up and cancellation, the regulation recognizes a simple truth: those who willingly joined a service should be able to leave it just as easily.
quick_facts: New York City enacted a click-to-cancel subscription rule
Cancellation must be as simple as signing up
Rule took effect to protect consumers from trapped contracts
